headings.text: What Would You Do To Create Your Forever Home?

restContentHtml:
While the start of a new year is often associated with making changes, many people in the UK have decided that one thing they’re not going to change in 2020 is their address. In fact, a growing number of homeowners appear to be deciding to make the best of where they live now.

Property Reporter shared the findings of a survey by LV= General Insurance, which revealed that 86 per cent of homeowners in the UK have decided to make changes to their current abode rather than moving somewhere new.

This equates to around 15 million people. The most popular way in which they’re making their home their own is to redecorate it in their own style. Over half (58 per cent) of those questioned said that this is what they intend to do in 2020.

Refurbishing the kitchen was the next most-popular renovation project to take on this year, with 50 per cent stating they’d do this, while 39 per cent said they’d focus their efforts on landscaping the garden.

The other two projects that made the top five, with 24 per cent each, were extending the house and painting its exterior.

Managing director of LV= General Insurance Direct business Heather Smith commented: “When looking to buy a property, especially one where you intend to stay put, it’s important to consider which factors are most important to you.”

If it’s living somewhere with period features, for example, you might want to consider how you can make the most of these, such as by investing in metal polishing in London to bring certain features back to their best.

But what if you haven’t found your forever home yet? Don’t worry as the survey revealed that people buy their forever home at an average age of 41, although many people who have yet to find their forever home believe they won’t buy it until they’re 49.

The research also found that over half (53 per cent) of people already live in their forever home.

It also revealed that the most important factor in a forever home is the garden, with 39 per cent of people citing this feature, while the number of bedrooms was second on the list, followed by access to amenities.

The Irish Times recently shared the results of the 2019 Houzz & Home Renovation Trends Study, which found that energy efficiency and using green materials in renovations are among the top considerations for homeowners making alterations to their properties.

As a result, the news provider made a number of recommendations of things that people can do to make their homes more energy efficient.

At the top of the list is switching to energy-efficient light bulbs, which is a low-cost measure and one that will not only save you energy but also reduce your electricity bills.

Replacing old windows for ones that are more thermally efficient is another suggestion, as is making sure that your attic is properly insulated to prevent heat from escaping through the roof.

When you’re planning to upgrade the insulation in your property, make sure you know how your home has been constructed and what insulation is already in place to ensure you make the most appropriate and safe changes, the news provider advised.
